translations.1b17c993053968565444739d: ⟪P0⟫At the end:⟪P1⟫ Build the report, the failure log, the triggers, and the supervision ritual for an agent, and turn every mistake into a rule.
translations.f7fa0db6a28a412c2c583c95: ⟪P0⟫1. The report you want to read⟪P1⟫
translations.9b11fbfa9cbe7539a901c24b: ⟪P0⟫2. Failure log: one line per error⟪P1⟫
translations.8e407696d0db1be9e1c7130d: ⟪P0⟫3. Triggers: when it pauses and calls you⟪P1⟫
translations.a13b08627404365d103114a0: ⟪P0⟫4. The ritual: 2 minutes per day, 10 per week, 1 review per month⟪P1⟫

translations.f540f2df7d6950250bef4103: The report you want to read
translations.04932e2ecac161eead5171f7: The report always has the same parts in the same order, and the errors section exists even when it’s empty.
translations.433e9ddf707e24d729dc2ccf: ⟪P0⟫Simple numbers⟪P1⟫3 to 5 counts you can understand at a glance.
translations.2dfdb24c230504ee135d037f: ⟪P0⟫Cases passed to you⟪P1⟫what needs human decision-making.
translations.25e1aa40267213561c846507: ⟪P0⟫Errors⟪P1⟫always in its own section, even if it’s “none.”
translations.5ea07e758eb77cb23063ffdb: ⟪P0⟫Fixed schedule⟪P1⟫every day or every week, always at the same time.
translations.77a5f21fe79e7e968e4736e5: ✓ Require the errors section to always be present, with “no errors” written when that’s the case.
translations.815871cc24d0deaa8b72d3a2: ✗ Ask for a long, pretty report no one reads, or one that only shows what went right.
translations.aedbb064f9c0038f0e21dbd7: Write the 4 counts you’d like to see in the daily report of a coordinator of volunteers at an NGO.
translations.14fea7ead0b9b7719bfb4131: Something like: confirmed shifts, rejections, substitutes found, and shifts still unfilled. The last one is the most important, because it’s the one that requires your action before the weekend ends. Good numbers point to a decision, not just volume.
translations.1877531d318866b5975f7230: Failure log: one line per error
translations.cbb15d2fd3db044b192a06d1: Each error goes through the same four columns, and the last one links the error to a concrete change in the agent sheet.
translations.178821c547d01b8b6644fff3: ⟪P0⟫What broke⟪P1⟫the fact, in one sentence, without blame.
translations.17ebdbfcdad990b005ad3570: ⟪P0⟫Smallest correction⟪P1⟫the smallest change that prevents the repetition.
translations.57363d23e07bf00b556f1767: ⟪P0⟫Rule changed⟪P1⟫which line in the agent sheet changed.
translations.3c44417764a8bbcf63496c9f: What broke: apply the decision described.
translations.bcce852bb63312b3d74d2551: Smallest correction: check the effect in the example.
translations.c801c4c5d1c30702d70ea9c6: Rule changed: record the output evidence.
translations.ee5a7a0d91875f7fb59026b9: ✓ Write the line on the same day as the error, before moving on to the next task.
translations.276d1f90b32a1ea5d882ac8c: ✗ Store the errors in memory and try to remember them only during the monthly review.
translations.0f0700f1ad38c6eefef34ce4: The store agent promised a customer a delivery date that wasn’t in the system. Write the log line.
translations.7abaf6dcad913ec01870b6ca: Example: ⟪P0⟫ · promised delivery date outside the system · only inform dates that are on the orders panel · Prohibitions earned “promising a date that is not in the system”. Notice that the correction is small and verifiable; it’s not “improving service”.
translations.bb728c15c2af55e9ad6e1f78: Triggers: when it pauses and calls you
translations.a52fc8b6c50ba626f5e8c446: The trigger interrupts the normal flow and returns the decision to the human before the error gets out of control.
translations.5878d02fc80b78aee81468b7: ⟪P0⟫Concrete⟪P1⟫something the agent can recognize without interpreting.
translations.eadc84e32307e78210256308: ⟪P0⟫Clear action⟪P1⟫it pauses, informs you, and doesn’t try to solve it.
